18 A car of weight 15 000 N is travelling along a horizontal road.
velocity
24 m s–1
resistive force
thrust force
3000 N
12 000 N
At one instant, the thrust force acting on the car from the engine is 12 000 N and the resistive
force acting on the car is 3000 N. The velocity of the car at this instant is 24 m s–1.
What is the power output from the engine?
A
72 kW
B
220 kW
C
290 kW
D
360 kW

hints: Notice the three separate forces: $12000\text{ N}$ forward thrust, $3000\text{ N}$ backward resistive force, and $15000\text{ N}$ downward weight at $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
Recall that power from a force along motion is $P = Fv$, so decide which force is actually supplied by the engine.
Check whether you need the thrust alone, the resistive force alone, or the resultant $12000-3000\text{ N}$ for engine output, then multiply by $24\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
walkthrough: Identify the useful data: engine thrust $F = 12000\text{ N}$ forward, car velocity $v = 24\text{ m s}^{-1}$ forward. The $3000\text{ N}$ resistive force and $15000\text{ N}$ weight do not drive the car.
State the rule for power from a force parallel to velocity: $P = Fv$.
The engine must provide power through its own thrust, so use $F = 12000\text{ N}$, not the net force $9000\text{ N}$ and not the weight.
Substitute with units: $P = 12000\text{ N} \times 24\text{ m s}^{-1} = 288000\text{ N m s}^{-1}$.
Convert to kilowatts: $288000\text{ W} = 288\text{ kW} \approx 290\text{ kW}$, which matches the power output. This is option C.

A.explanation: This is $3000 \times 24 = 72\text{ kW}$, the power dissipated against the $3000\text{ N}$ resistive force, not the power supplied by the engine thrust.

B.explanation: This is $(12000-3000) \times 24 = 216\text{ kW}$, the net power that increases kinetic energy, not the total power output from the $12000\text{ N}$ engine thrust.

C.explanation: Engine power is $12000 \times 24 = 288000\text{ W} \approx 290\text{ kW}$ using the thrust force in the direction of motion.

D.explanation: This is $15000 \times 24 = 360\text{ kW}$, which wrongly uses the vertical $15000\text{ N}$ weight instead of the forward thrust force.
